pacing.coverage: Six recordings (the update's original time against its 28 MHz time); JNext 1.2.0 stage 1, 300 updates keyed to updates against the unpatched build. Stages 2-5 not measured in JNext.
pacing.result: About 5.6 updates a second; per-update deadline P = 8.02 x (D + credit) + 645 lines plus frame waits (D without the present's copy, as measured; credit = the time the sprite fast path saved); the gap before it holds up to 4-5 in-between frames; music owned by the interrupt handler (550 AY writes a second, unchanged).

dependencies.coverage: Write set of the update (W, 21 ranges) and the bytes shared with the handler (X, 139 bytes) from the recordings; V2 over 400 captured states and every 25th update of five stages checks nothing else changes.
dependencies.result: The update's writes are restored after each in-between frame; the handler keeps the real values; R differs only through hook instructions (random numbers, verification exception).

feasibility.decision: Owner's brief 2026-11-21 (smoothness, autonomous): the real update at 28 MHz paced to the original, the gap filled with run-ahead in-between frames of the game's own drawing.
feasibility.next_experiment: Hardware: smooth road at speed in stage 1 and the five stage loads with no tape; pace within 2% of the original over 300 updates.

verify.note: Every 25th race update of each recording: V1 the real update (in-between frames off) against the original with R supplied, V2 in-between frames on against off (registers, all RAM outside the masks, sound ports, return time); unit tests: six stage loads, negative W and R controls. Pace and flicker are in games/cisco_heat.md "Evidence".
